clue.text: What tennis players may be doing in the forces

definitions.text: What tennis players may be doing
definitions.meaning: a tennis player puts the ball into play from the baseline at the start of each point
someone in the army, navy or air force is said to be on active duty in uniform

explanation.surface: A question about what tennis players get up to while enlisted in the military.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both putting a tennis ball into play and doing duty as a member of the armed forces.

clue.text: Demand for the whole nation to go in fun sports event!

definitions.text: Demand for the whole nation to go
definitions.meaning: read as a command: dismiss (...) the entire people (...)
a jokey school sports-day contest where runners hop along inside bags

explanation.surface: An exclamation calling for a whole country to leave, set beside a jolly sports day.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as an order, 'sack the race' demands that a whole people be fired; read as a noun phrase it is the sports-day event where children hop in bags.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a children's sports-day contest in hessian bags and, read literally, orders a whole people dismissed.

clue.text: See 1
Fashionable carriage, for example

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
carriage here is posture, the way one holds oneself, so stance

explanation.surface: A smart horse-drawn vehicle offered as an illustration of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' suggests a vehicle, but here it means bearing or posture.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a single case cited to illustrate something is a specimen or illustration of it.

clue.text: Dynamic chaps with energy moving bush

indicators.note: moving says one letter of the word for the chaps is shifted to a new place

parts.note: goers are lively, energetic people
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Energetic men are relocating a shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' shifts the E of GOERS from the middle to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse is a spiny yellow-flowered shrub of heaths and moorland, so a kind of bush.

clue.text: Whacking hostile delivery at the Oval?

definitions.meaning: whacking here is an adjective meaning huge, as in a whacking great crop
in cricket a short ball that rears up at the batsman's head; the Oval is a London cricket ground

explanation.surface: Hitting a menacing ball during a cricket match at the Oval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whacking' looks like hitting, but it is the adjective meaning very large.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means exceptionally large, as in a bumper harvest, and is the cricket term for a fast short-pitched ball aimed at the body.

clue.text: Bare man swimming in river

indicators.note: in says the jumbled letters go inside the river's name

parts.note: the Usk is a river in Wales

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters of man moving about freely

explanation.surface: A naked man swimming in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bare' looks like an adjective describing the swimmer, but it is a verb meaning expose.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to bare a person or plot is to expose them by removing a disguise.

clue.text: Promotion before commotion

parts.note: pre is the prefix meaning before
ferment means agitation or turmoil

explanation.surface: A rhyming maxim about getting a promotion ahead of upheaval.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: advancement to a higher rank or office, especially in the church.

clue.text: Reformed characters in parishes do wax lyrical

indicators.note: reformed says the letters are re-formed into a new shape, apt beside the church sense

explanation.surface: Reformed people in parishes get lyrical about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' rearranges the letters of PARISHES DO.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom match: to speak or write with great enthusiasm and emotion, like an ecstatic poem.

clue.text: Swaggering, make better boxing punch first to last

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the cure word goes round the punch

parts.note: to cure is to heal

indicators.note: first to last means the opening letter of the punch word moves to its end

parts.note: a sock is a punch

explanation.surface: A swaggering boxer improves by throwing a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' looks like the sport in this boxer's picture, but it signals one piece enclosing another.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: overconfident and arrogant in manner.

clue.text: In old Rome I love retiring president, a low form of life

parts.note: amo is Latin for I love

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Abe Lincoln was a US president

explanation.surface: In ancient Rome someone declares love for a president who is stepping down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' reverses ABE to EBA.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoeba is a single-celled organism, the stock example of a primitive creature.

clue.text: Cheerful servant good for morose leader

indicators.note: good for morose leader means G takes the place of the first letter of morose

parts.note: a menial is a domestic servant

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word morose

explanation.surface: A happy servant is good at replacing a gloomy boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' picks M from morose; 'for' puts G in its place in MENIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: friendly and warmly good-humoured.

clue.text: Pat kindly covers up the foreign head's negligence

indicators.note: covers up means the stroking word wraps around the French article

parts.note: to caress is to stroke gently
le is French for the
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A kindly pat hides a foreign boss's negligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' reads as a boss, but here it is a headland, a geographical promontory.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a failure to take proper care or attention.

clue.text: Trouble afoot — temperature's cold in the Land of More Plenty

parts.note: a corn is a painful patch on the foot

indicators.note: temperature's cold in the land means that inside it the T letter becomes C

parts.note: Thomas More wrote Utopia, about an ideal land
T is the abbreviation for temperature
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Foot trouble and a cold snap in an ideal land of abundance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' looks like 'extra', but it is Sir Thomas More, author of Utopia; changing its T to C gives UCOPIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The horn of plenty is a symbol of abundance, so the word stands for a plentiful supply.

clue.text: Purchasing power of earnings in Brazil?

definitions.text: Purchasing power of earnings in Brazil?

parts.words: Purchasing power of earnings in Brazil?
parts.note: the real is Brazil's currency, so earnings there would be paid in reals

explanation.surface: An economist asks what wages actually buy in Brazil.
explanation.walkthrough: Economists' term for pay adjusted for inflation; the question mark points to the Brazilian currency, the real.
explanation.definitionFit: The economists' term for income measured by what it will actually buy after inflation.

clue.text: Remaining board members (one third gone) promise too much

parts.note: over means left remaining, as in food left over

indicators.note: one third gone means the final three of the nine letters are dropped

parts.note: a committee is a board of members

explanation.surface: The remaining board members, a third having left, make too many promises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one third gone' cuts the last three letters (TEE) from COMMITTEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to pledge more time or resources than one can actually deliver.

clue.text: Doctor's sobriety half-gone — either half

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

indicators.note: half-gone says the first four of its eight letters are lost

explanation.surface: A doctor whose sobriety is half gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-gone' drops SOBR from SOBRIETY, leaving IETY.
explanation.definitionFit: A moiety is a half share, one of two equal parts of something.

clue.text: Malicious utterance damaging leaders, perhaps

indicators.note: leaders means the first letter of each of the three preceding words

explanation.surface: Spiteful words harming political leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes M, U and D from the first three words; the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Slander is called this, as in mud-slinging: spiteful talk meant to damage reputations.

clue.text: Crowd trouble on the rise after a cricketer's shambles

indicators.note: after says the reversed trouble word follows the cricketer

parts.note: a bat is a batsman, a cricketer

indicators.note: on the rise in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a riot is trouble from a crowd

explanation.surface: Crowd trouble follows after a cricketer's performance turns into a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rise' reverses RIOT to TOIR. 'Shambles' means a slaughterhouse, its original sense, not a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sense: a shambles was a meat market or slaughterhouse, which is what the answer names.

clue.text: Endless row over nothing

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the shortened word is read backwards
endless says the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a line is a row

explanation.surface: An unending argument about nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts LINE to LIN, and 'over' reverses it. 'Row' looks like a quarrel but means a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: zero, used especially in sports scores.

clue.text: All gibbons gathered in distant watering holes

indicators.note: gathered suggests the creatures bunching together, so their letters are regrouped

explanation.surface: All the apes gather at faraway drinking spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered' rearranges ALL GIBBONS. 'Distant' because these are Australian.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia, a stagnant pool left by a river, where animals come to drink.

clue.text: Soldier guarding modern artist's house, one of 12

indicators.note: guarding means the soldier surrounds what he protects

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
Tracey Emin is a contemporary British artist

explanation.surface: A soldier stands guard over a contemporary artist's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' is an astrological house: Gemini is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrologers divide the zodiac into twelve houses or signs, and the Twins are one of them.

clue.text: Band of players celebrate after work for soloists curtailed

indicators.note: after says the celebration word follows the musical work
curtailed means the tail, the final letter, is cut off

parts.note: a concerto is a work for soloist and orchestra
to party is to celebrate

explanation.surface: Musicians celebrate after a shortened concerto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' cuts CONCERTO to CONCERT.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe of entertainers giving a variety show, as at a seaside resort or for troops.

clue.text: Watch chain not originally belonging on watch?

indicators.note: not says the picked letter is taken away

parts.note: an albert is a pocket-watch chain, named after Prince Albert

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of belonging

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a watch chain belongs on a watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' picks B from belonging and 'not' removes it from ALBERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being vigilant, like a sentry keeping guard, is being wide awake to danger.

clue.text: Fringes of more stylish network

indicators.note: fringes are the edges, so the first and last letters of each word

explanation.surface: The edges of a more fashionable net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fringes of' takes M and E from more, and S and H from stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an interlaced net of threads or wires.

clue.text: Film company dismissing one old boss

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so the letters are removed

parts.note: a studio is a film company
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A film company fires one of its veteran bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is a knob or raised ornament, not a manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised knob or ornamental button, like the round metal knob on a belt.

clue.text: Unorthodox bishop with answer for society's hatred

indicators.note: unorthodox suggests the bishop going off the doctrinal path, so the letters are rearranged
answer for society means the A letter takes the place of the S

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A heretical bishop answers for the hatred in society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' turns BISHOP into BIAHOP, and 'Unorthodox' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: An irrational fear or strong aversion to something, close to loathing.

clue.text: Suggestive payment made to landlord in receipt of benefit

indicators.note: in receipt of means holding, so the payment word goes round the benefit

parts.note: rent is paid to a landlord
the dole is British state unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: A tenant pays rent while claiming benefits.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: evocative, as in a place reminiscent of a bygone age.

clue.text: Vinegary old hermit's no saint

indicators.note: no says the saint is absent, so that letter is removed

parts.note: an ascetic is a hermit who lives in self-denial

explanation.surface: A sour old recluse is far from saintly.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic acid is the sour component of vinegar, so the adjective means vinegar-like.

clue.text: Rubbish written about church — editor fired

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the rubbish word is read backwards

parts.note: rot is nonsense

explanation.surface: An editor fires off nonsense about the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses ROT to TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: set alight deliberately, as a building set ablaze by arsonists.
